context: Method selection for additional direct connectivity that is neither VPN nor application proxy.

records.claim: zapret supports separate multi-strategy profiles with --new, protocol/port filters, hostlists, and direct desync methods for HTTP/TLS/QUIC.
Official zapret guidance favors intercepting the minimum required traffic; hostlist scoping is therefore retained.
records.evidence: Official zapret readme and quick-start; existing project hostlist model.

records.claim: Use four direct families in v1.4.0: IP-bootstrapped DoH, HTTP/80 host split, TLS/SNI TCP/443 desync, QUIC UDP/443 desync.
records.evidence: Existing pinned ctrld/zapret capabilities + Linux nfqws --dry-run PASS for the three packet profiles.

records.claim: Do not enable IP fragmentation by default.
records.evidence: Official zapret docs state modern networks are hostile to fragmentation; TCP fragments are almost always filtered and UDP fragment survival is not universal.

records.claim: Do not enable wssize/window tricks by default.
records.evidence: Official zapret docs warn wssize may slow sites/increase response time and recommend other working methods when possible.

records.claim: Keep current IP-bootstrapped DoH rather than adding DoH3/DoQ/DoT solely for feature count.
records.evidence: ctrld officially supports doh/doh3/dot/doq/legacy, while the current DoH path already has project live evidence; no evidence currently justifies added fallback complexity.
records.supersededReason: Official ctrld docs show desktop leak_on_upstream_failure defaults true and ordered encrypted upstream retry is supported; the user explicitly requested additional non-VPN/non-proxy methods.

records.claim: Do not add a second DPI-bypass binary such as GoodbyeDPI; existing pinned zapret covers the required direct techniques.
Linux nfqws v72.13 accepted the proposed TCP80/TCP443/UDP443 multi-profile command with --dry-run and the current six-host list.
records.evidence: aliemad-Labtop command-line dry-run, exit 0; 3 user-defined profiles; 6 hosts loaded.

records.claim: Windows pinned winws binary contains all required multiprotocol option strings; execution of winws itself requires elevation on this host.
records.evidence: binary option-string audit on Emad-PC-Ultimate; non-elevated --dry-run blocked by executable elevation requirement.

records.claim: DoH3, DoQ and DoT were evaluated as additional encrypted-DNS transports but are not enabled in v1.4.0 because isolated current-network tests did not resolve successfully; established direct-IP DoH remained successful.
records.evidence: aliemad-Labtop isolated ctrld v1.5.7 tests: DoH to 76.76.10.11/p0 PASS; DoH3, DoQ, DoT returned no DNS answer; alternate direct-IP DoH 76.76.2.11 also returned no answer. Official ctrld docs confirm all transports are supported by software, so the limitation is environmental/evidence-based rather than parser capability.

records.claim: ECH is not implemented as a Direct Internet Method toggle because it is browser/server negotiated; Firefox enables it by default where supported and it relies on encrypted DNS HTTPS records.
records.evidence: Mozilla ECH documentation and Cloudflare ECH documentation.

records.claim: Alternative ctrld secure DNS transports were live-tested non-disruptively on aliemad-Labtop before inclusion: current-network results were DoH PASS, DoH3 FAIL timeout, DoQ FAIL, DoT FAIL.
records.evidence: Ephemeral ctrld listeners on high local ports with dig queries to www.youtube.com; no system DNS mutation.

records.claim: DoH3/DoQ/DoT fallback is not enabled in v1.4.0 because three alternatives failed on the current network while direct IP-bootstrapped DoH passed; adding them would increase timeout/failover latency without demonstrated availability.
records.evidence: Current-network transport matrix plus official ctrld support documentation.

records.claim: v1.4.0 sets ctrld leak_on_upstream_failure=false so encrypted-DNS upstream failure does not silently fall back to the physical OS resolver.
records.evidence: Official ctrld config docs state leak_on_upstream_failure defaults true on Windows, macOS and non-router Linux; project goal requires direct encrypted DNS rather than filtered physical DNS fallback.

exactNextAction: Rebuild Windows manifest/payload and Linux archive, pass source/build gates, then live-validate the exact v1.4.0 Linux protected backend Start/Stop/Recovery before publication.

concurrentMutation.observed: Uncommitted windows/bin/ctrld/ctrld.toml mutation attempted DoH→DoH3→DoQ→DoT failover and leak_on_upstream_failure=false.
concurrentMutation.rationale: Mutation appeared after the v1.4 Windows artifact build, was not part of the controlled change set, and live transport testing did not support DoH3/DoQ/DoT availability on the current network. Baseline direct-IP DoH remains authoritative.
